chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Zarif ibn Nasih, from Ibrahim ibn Yahya, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both), who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

God, the Blessed and Exalted, divided the people of the earth into two groups, and placed me in the better of the two. Then He divided the other half into three, and I was the best of the three. Then He chose the Arabs from among the people, then He chose Quraysh from among the Arabs, then He chose Banu Hashim from among Quraysh, then He chose Banu Abd al-Muttalib from among Banu Hashim, then He chose me from among Banu Abd al-Muttalib.
ai.seo_question: What is the divine selection process of the Prophet Muhammad according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal articulates the Shia doctrine of *Takhassus* (divine selection), presenting a hierarchical cosmology where God progressively narrows His choice from all humanity to the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) through specific lineages. It underscores the theological necessity of the Prophet's unique status and the purity of the Ahl al-Bayt, serving as a foundational text for understanding the spiritual hierarchy (*Imamah*) in Shia Islam. The narrative reinforces the idea that prophethood and imamate are not merely political appointments but divinely ordained spiritual realities rooted in creation.
